series: Things Living In Your House, Part 22
sources: Connecticut Agricultural Experiment Station, House Centipede fact sheet (K. Dugas): nocturnal; fast runners that chase prey; flees when discovered; frequents basements, cellars and first-floor bathrooms; most are never seen; venomous forcipules sting prey; stinging a human is very rare, only from rough handling; hunts bed bugs and cockroach nymphs; reduce humidity and exclude the insects they prey on; antennae look like legs; 15 pairs of legs; upwards of 3 years to mature, can live up to 7 years; https://portal.ct.gov/-/media/caes/documents/publications/fact_sheets/entomology/house_centipede_scutigera.pdf
Penn State Extension, House Centipedes: comes out at night; feeds on silverfish, carpet beetle larvae, cockroaches, spiders; harmless; https://extension.psu.edu/house-centipedes
Washington State University Extension PestSense, House centipede: usually active at night; https://pestsense.cahnrs.wsu.edu/fact-sheet/house-centipede/

title: Turn On Your Bathroom Light at 3 A.M.
tiktok_caption: house centipede part 3 🐛 turn on the light at 3am and this is who's working the night shift. Would you flip the switch? 💡 yes / 🙈 never

beats.say: Turn on your bathroom light at three A.M.
That blur running for the drain? Thirty legs.
It works the night shift. Hunting roaches.
Its feelers look like legs. Which end is the face?
Turn it off. Let it work.
It's a house centipede, and it hunts at night.
It's a fast runner. It chases down its food.
Silverfish, spiders, cockroaches, carpet beetle larvae.
When you flip on the light, it runs. It doesn't want you.
That's why most people never see theirs.
By day it hides in basements, cellars and bathrooms.
Its long feelers look just like legs.
So a predator can't tell which end is the face.
Fifteen pairs of legs. About three years to grow up.
And it can live up to seven years. In your house.
Bug experts say it's harmless to people.
It stings its prey with legs that turned into fangs.
Will it sting you? Almost never. Only if you grab it hard.
It even eats bed bugs and baby cockroaches.
Want fewer of them? Dry out the damp spots.
The bugs it eats move out, and so does it.
Even silverfish and moths. It eats the bugs you hate.
It would rather run than fight you.
So next time, turn the light off and let it work. Would you?
Follow me. Next: the bug living in your bed.
